video.title: How to Start a Business? Don’t Wait for Permission.

summary: Chris Koerner speaks to a homeschool class of about 20 high schoolers, telling his story from selling washed golf balls at age 10 to iPhone repair stores, an LCD screen recycling business and a failed mobile home park venture. He answers Q&A on starting with no money, validating demand by selling before building (Facebook Marketplace, a tree trimming ad test), business partnerships, and his marketing-heavy, operations-light approach. The key takeaway is to sell something before doing 'procrastination' tasks like LLCs and websites, and to use constraints as a source of creativity.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Serial entrepreneur and creator of The Koerner Office, speaking to a homeschool class

ideas.name: Washed golf ball roadside stand
ideas.one_liner: Collect golf balls that land in the yard, wash them and sell three for a dollar to golfers from a stand outside the house.
ideas.business_model: One-off product sales of found, cleaned goods
ideas.customer: Golfers walking past a golf course on a busy road
ideas.problem: Not stated beyond golfers wanting cheap golf balls

acquisition_channels.details: Plywood sign leaning on mailbox on a busy road across from a golf course; golfers walked up and knocked.

ideas.delivery: Child washed balls and sold from a wagon at the house.
unit_economics_claims: Made hundreds of dollars a summer, week or month (he does not remember)

uk_applicability.notes: Depends on living next to a golf course, supply of stray balls and a busy road; tiny scale and not agent-runnable.

quotes.text: I put golf balls, three for a dollar. And I leaned this sign up against my mailbox. It was a really busy road.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Textbook Crook student textbook marketplace
ideas.one_liner: Website for students to buy and sell textbooks to each other instead of accepting low bookstore buyback prices.
ideas.problem: Bookstores sell textbooks at about $200 and buy them back for about $20.
ideas.offer: Peer-to-peer textbook buy and sell website
unit_economics_claims: Bookstore sold at $200 and bought back for $20

acquisition.how: Would need campus marketing or SEO.

delivery.how: Software matching, but physical book exchange.

uk_applicability.notes: UK has Amazon, eBay and Facebook groups competing; textbook buyback gap is smaller.

quotes.text: I thought there needs to be a way for students to buy and sell textbooks to each other. And so that's why I started that website.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: iPhone repair stores
ideas.one_liner: Open physical iPhone screen repair stores, learning repairs from YouTube; grew to four stores and sold to a competitor.

acquisition_channels.details: Did some marketing; details not given in this talk.

ideas.delivery: Owner repaired phones in store, learning from YouTube.
unit_economics_claims: Raised $20,000 from a friend to start
Opened four stores over two years and sold to a competitor
ideas.startup_cost: $20,000 raised from a friend met on his mission

acquisition.how: Local SEO and Google Maps could work.

uk_applicability.notes: Repair shops exist in the UK but the 2010 opportunity is long gone and the market is crowded.

quotes.text: people would come in with broken iPhones and I would say, "Okay, it's $80." And then they leave. And then I'd learn how to fix the iPhone on YouTube while I fixed it.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: LCD Cycle broken screen recycling and parts supply
ideas.one_liner: Pay repair shops $3 per broken iPhone screen, ship them to China for remanufacture, and sell parts to those shops.
ideas.business_model: Parts sales to repair shops plus broken screen buyback and resale
ideas.problem: Repair shops have piles of broken screens and need cheap parts
ideas.offer: Buy their broken screens for $3 each and sell them parts

acquisition_channels.details: Used the screen buyback offer as a foot in the door with repair shops.

ideas.delivery: Ship broken screens to a Chinese remanufacturer, sell parts and ship from Texas.
unit_economics_claims: Business lasted 9 years and grew very fast

acquisition.how: Cold email to repair shops (mostly limited companies) is feasible.

uk_applicability.notes: UK repair shops exist but import, WEEE and logistics rules apply; margins uncertain.

risks: Founder copied an existing company's idea

quotes.text: we'll pay you $3 for every broken iPhone screen." And they were like, "Why do you want my broken screens?"
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Mobile home and RV park investing
ideas.one_liner: Bought mobile home and RV parks with partners; ended badly and he lost everything.

uk_applicability.notes: Mobile home parks are a different regime in the UK.

quotes.text: I had two partners that I didn't get to know well enough and it went south and lost everything.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Tree trimming lead-gen business with subcontractors
ideas.one_liner: Test demand with a Facebook Marketplace ad, generate customers, and subcontract all work to tree crews with no owned equipment.
ideas.problem: Need tree work quoted and done
ideas.offer: Tree trimming services, fulfilled by subcontract crews

price_points.label: higher-ticket home service example (tree trimming or landscaping)

pricing.notes: Contrasted with about $40 for a lawn mowing job.

acquisition_channels.details: Posted a tree trimming ad on Facebook Marketplace before doing anything else; got quote requests within five minutes.

quote.text: Five minutes later, hey, can you come to my house and quote the shop?
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.delivery: Subcontracted tree trimming crews; the business owns no chainsaws or equipment.
unit_economics_claims: About $3,000 per job vs $40 for lawn job
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Demand shown within minutes of posting ad

acquisition.how: Marketplace and local ads automatable, plus SEO and Google Business Profile.

delivery.how: Subcontractors do physical work; coordination can be agent-assisted.

uk_applicability.notes: Works in the UK via Facebook Marketplace, Checkatrade and Google; need insurance and subcontractor vetting, tree preservation orders.

quotes.text: we launched a tree trimming business and I posted an ad on Facebook Marketplace for a tree trimming services before we did anything.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

quotes.text: we don't own a chainsaw. We don't own any equipment. We subcontract everything out to tree trimming crews. We just go find the customers.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Door-to-door window washing
ideas.one_liner: Quote neighbours' windows per window, take payment up front, buy supplies with part of it and clean the same day.
ideas.offer: Window washing, free quote, same-day service

acquisition_channels.details: Knock on neighbour's door, offer free quote, collect money up front.

ideas.startup_cost: About $50 of supplies from the first job's deposit

uk_applicability.notes: Window cleaning is established in the UK; door knocking is legal but leafleting and online booking work too.

quotes.text: You take that 250 bucks. You go to Home Depot. Use 50 of it to buy supplies. You come back, wash the windows, you have $200 profit
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Facebook Marketplace reselling for a cut
ideas.one_liner: Kids list and sell household items on Facebook Marketplace for 40% of the sale, learning selling and demand testing.
ideas.business_model: Commission on resale of household items
ideas.problem: Families have items to sell but dislike selling
ideas.offer: Handle photos, listing, pricing, communication and handover

acquisition_channels.details: List items on Facebook Marketplace with video first, researched sold prices, fast responses.

ideas.delivery: Take photos, list with AI-generated descriptions, research sold prices, meet buyer at door.

acquisition.how: Listing and replies can be tool-assisted.

uk_applicability.notes: Facebook Marketplace, eBay and Vinted work in the UK.

quotes.text: I pay my kids 40% to sell anything that I allow them to sell.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Solo cup nostalgia products
ideas.one_liner: Illustrative brainstorm: candles in solo cups, Etsy artwork, T-shirts, or a solo-cup-look insulated tumbler.
ideas.offer: Solo cup themed candles, art, shirts, tumblers

uk_applicability.notes: Solo cups are less iconic in the UK; trademark and IP risk.

risks: Ideas untested, he says they might not be good

quotes.text: nostalgia sells. People will pay a lot of money for nostalgia. And so you could make candles where this is like the vessel that holds the wax
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Lawn care business
ideas.one_liner: Considered a lawn care business but dropped it; says it is low ticket and price-competitive compared with tree trimming or landscaping.

acquisition_channels.details: Printed flyers and put them on doors in a neighbourhood.

unit_economics_claims: $40 per lawn job vs $3,000 for tree trimming or landscaping

uk_applicability.notes: Gardening services are common in the UK.

quotes.text: it's a great business to start, but it's tough because it's low ticket. You can't charge a lot.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Koerner Office content and media
ideas.one_liner: Publishes content on Twitter, Instagram, Facebook, TikTok about business ideas he tries; grew quickly over about three years.
ideas.problem: People want business ideas and encouragement

acquisition_channels.details: Started with Twitter account, added video a year ago.

quotes.text: about three years ago, I started talking about everything I'd ever done in business on the internet. And it grew really fast.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Sell it before you have it
steps: Pick an idea and offer it to someone before building anything
Aim for even $1 of revenue before LLC, website, business plan
Try to get a non-friend or non-family customer to pay

quote.text: Sell it before you have it.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Test demand with a Facebook Marketplace ad
steps: Post an ad for the service before buying equipment
Count inbound quote requests
Only invest if demand shows up
Subcontract delivery rather than buy gear

quote.text: there's so many things we can do to test the market, test the demand before ever spending a dollar.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Collect payment up front to self-fund a service business
steps: Offer a free quote
Take payment before or on the job
Use part of the money to buy supplies
Keep the remainder as profit

quote.text: You can collect money up front. You could do a service business that requires no hardware or materials at all.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Use door-to-door sales as a testing lab
steps: Knock on hundreds of doors
Vary one thing at a time such as smile, greeting, introduction
Refine script until it converts

quote.text: If you knock on a 100 doors, that's a 100 different tests.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Facebook Marketplace selling checklist
steps: Take photos and put a video first
Use AI to generate the description
Check sold listings for pricing
Respond quickly
Meet buyer and accept payment

quote.text: put a video first, it will get more traction, do the market research on pricing, looked at the sold items, be very responsive
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Partnership equity structure
steps: Be 50/50 only if both are full-time, all-in and side by side in person
Otherwise use 90/10 or 80/20 weighted splits
Pick a partner whose strengths cover your weaknesses

quote.text: In any other circumstance, 50/50 is a disaster waiting to happen.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Marketing-heavy, operations-light model
steps: Focus on finding customers
Subcontract operations
Exit day-to-day once launched and showing traction

quote.text: my businesses I try to get out of the business as soon as I can once it's launched and it shows traction.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Do not wait for LLC, website or business plan before selling; it is disguised procrastination.

quote.text: we do these things that give us the illusion of productivity without actually doing the thing.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Entrepreneurship is volatile, with years of zero income.

quote.text: It's just a roller coaster, feast or famine.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Take advice only from relevant experienced people or people with nothing to lose; filter advice from others.

lessons.lesson: Opportunities close to you are the ones you notice; the golf ball business came only from living across from a course.

quote.text: a lot of times the best opportunities are the ones around us because it's the ones that we notice
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Earning your first money without a job changes your mindset and builds independence, like food storage for your bank account.

quote.text: having a skill where you don't have to depend on an employer is kind of like food storage for your bank account.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Starting before you know the skill works, but you must then learn it; he says not learning more was his mistake.
Mass rejection (40-50k doors in Hungary) builds confidence and sales skill.

quote.text: I got rejected like 40 to 50,000 times in two years.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Constraints drive creativity; heavily funded companies are more likely to fail because they never need to be creative.

quote.text: constraints equal creativity.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Don't take things at face value; small tweaks (paying a stranger in line to buy a shirt) solve problems.
Complement your weaknesses with partners rather than spending years fixing them; he is strong at zero-to-one and weak at operations.
As you gain experience, filter ideas for best use of time instead of building every idea.
Higher-ticket home services beat low-ticket ones for the same effort.

quote.text: You can do the same amount of work or less with a home service that's higher ticket
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Persistence and willingness to pivot are the core success traits.

quote.text: you never finish where you start. So, never be afraid to pivot and to adapt
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

evidence_quality.rationale: Informal talk to students: first-hand anecdotes but few specific numbers; most figures are hypothetical or vague (golf ball earnings unremembered, no results for most businesses).
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Koerner sells content/audience influence and has ownership in about 12 businesses; no specific product pitched here.
